calibre3d.title: Calibre3D
calibre3d.text: Calibre3D The Calibre3D profile is for the calibre3d project: a Python program that measures pieces with a RealSense camera. It is meant for people who have never used a terminal: choose the project's folder once, press one button, and everything it needs is installed. Using it Choose Calibre3D in the profile selector. Press Elegir carpeta and choose the folder of the calibre3d project (the one that holds the calibre3d package and prueba.sh ). It is remembered. Press Preparar entorno . The installation shows on the right, line by line. When it ends, the status turns Listo . Which requirements file is installed The camera library has a different name on each computer, so there is one requirements file per platform. Preparar entorno installs the first of these the project has: This computer's own file: requirements-macos.txt on a Mac, requirements-linux.txt anywhere else. requirements.txt . The Entorno card says which one ("Se instalará requirements-macos.txt."). A project can carry both platform files and work on both computers; an old requirements.txt that only works on Linux is then ignored on the Mac without touching it. When the project has none, the card says "Sin requirements.txt: se usará la plantilla de macOS" (or Linux), and Preparar entorno first writes that computer's template into the project and then installs it. Package requirements-linux.txt requirements-macos.txt Why numpy>=1.24 ✓ ✓ Point clouds and depth images. scipy>=1.10 ✓ ✓ Fitting the plane, segmenting and measuring the piece. matplotlib>=3.7 ✓ ✓ The thickness heat maps and the views (PNG). pyrealsense2>=2.55 ✓ The RealSense camera; Ver cámara and Guardar imagen need it too. pyrealsense2-macosx>=2.56 ✓ (Apple silicon only) The same camera library. Intel publishes no macOS wheels, so pyrealsense2 cannot be installed on a Mac at all; this community build imports the same way ( import pyrealsense2 ) and needs macOS 15 or later. On an Intel Mac the camera line's condition ( platform_machine == "arm64" ) skips it, and the rest still works ( Demo sin cámara included). A requirements file that lists no packages (only comments or blank lines) installs nothing and skips pip, so it needs no internet. The Plantilla Linux and Plantilla macOS buttons write those templates into the project without installing, to add to the project's repository or to compare. They never overwrite a file: if it already exists they say so and leave it as it is. The status Status Means What to do 🔴 Sin proyecto No folder chosen, or it is gone. Press Elegir carpeta . 🔴 Sin entorno The folder has no .venv . Press Preparar entorno . 🟠 Incompleto .venv exists, but import calibre3d fails in it. Read the reason under the status (below). When the environment is incomplete, the card says why, from what Python answered: Reason shown Means En esta carpeta no está el programa calibre3d The folder chosen is not the one with the calibre3d package: choose the project's folder, the one with prueba.sh . Esta carpeta tiene prueba.sh pero le falta la carpeta calibre3d/ The right folder, but only prueba.sh was copied: copy the whole project, calibre3d/ included. Falta la librería X: añade Y a requirements.txt calibre3d imports a library that is not installed; Y is its pip name ( cv2 → opencv-python ). Error al cargar calibre3d: … Another error while importing; the text is Python's last line. 🟢 Listo import calibre3d works in .venv . The status is checked when the profile is first shown, when a folder is chosen, when an installation ends, and when you press Comprobar . It is not checked on every frame: the check starts Python once, which takes a moment. What "Preparar entorno" does In the project folder, one after the other, stopping at the first that fails: python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-macos.txt # or -linux, or requirements.txt The file is picked as described above; without any it writes the template first. With one that lists no packages it only creates .venv and says there was nothing to install. An existing .venv is reused, not deleted. Pressing it again on a ready environment ( Volver a preparar ) installs whatever is missing. It needs an internet connection. The environment is always made with the launcher's own Python 3.12 on Linux (x86-64, ARM) and macOS (Apple silicon, Intel), so every computer runs the same, tested version. The Python card, the first one, shows whether it is installed and offers Instalar Python 3.12 ; while it is missing that is the primary button and Preparar entorno is a quiet one, and pressing Preparar entorno anyway downloads Python first. The download is a ready-made Python from python-build-standalone : no installer and no password. Its checksum is pinned in internal/domain/python_download.go , so a damaged or altered file is refused, and it is unpacked through a sibling folder, so a cut connection never leaves a half-installed Python. It lives in python-3.12.15/ inside the config folder ( ~/.config/script-launcher/ on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/script-launcher/ on macOS) and every project uses it. On any other computer the card is hidden and the computer's own python3 is used (on macOS the python.org or Homebrew one; Apple's /usr/bin/python3 does not count, since without the developer tools it only opens a dialog). Calibrating and measuring Once the status is Listo , the Medir card runs calibre3d's steps in order, each with what to do before pressing it: Button Runs Do first 1. Plano python -m calibre3d plano Leave the mat empty. Once done, it says when and how noisy ("Hecho el 1 nov, 22:10 · ruido 0,04 mm"), from datos/plano.json . 2. Centrar python -m calibre3d centrar Put a coin on the cross. Its output says how far to move the mat; centrado_vista.png shows under it. 3. Patrón python -m calibre3d patron <name> --real L A E Put a piece of known size inside the circle. It asks for the pattern's name and its real length, width and thickness in mm (decimal point or comma). Beside the button: "Sin calibrar", or how many patterns there are and the correction they give ("2 patrones · L,A ×1,0012 +0,95 mm · E ×1,0000 +0,02 mm"), from datos/calibracion.json . patron_<name>_vista.png shows under its output. 4. Medir python -m calibre3d medir <name> Put the piece inside the circle. It asks for the piece's name (letters, digits, - , _ ); a name already measured is refused, so no result is overwritten. Without a plane it says "Haz primero el plano", but lets you go on, as calibre3d does. Demo sin cámara python -m calibre3d demo Nothing: it measures a simulated piece, to try everything without the camera. While a step runs, its output shows live in Actividad and the other steps, the photo and the camera wait. The live camera is closed before each step (with a notice), since calibre3d needs the camera alone. When Medir or the demo ends well, the launcher reads the result file calibre3d left ( datos/resultados/<name>.json , or demo/resultados/demo_canto.json ) and shows a strip at the top of Actividad with the length, width, thickness and maximum Feret diameter, and calibre3d's warnings. It stays there, whatever runs next, until another measurement replaces it. Under the output come the heat map ( _mapa.png ) and the view ( _vista.png ). If a step fails, its error shows in red under Actividad and the last result stays as it was. plantilla (the mat's PDF) is not a button yet: run it from a terminal in the project folder. Calibrating with patterns Without a calibration, calibre3d shows what it measured as it is, and with a real camera the length and width tend to come out slightly short (the bottom of a rounded edge is below the 0.3 mm threshold and the camera smooths the edges). 3. Patrón corrects that: calibre3d measures a piece whose real sizes you typed, adds it to datos/calibracion.json and fits real = k·measured + b again; every later Medir applies it on its own (the demo never does). The correction is only as good as the real sizes: measure the patterns with a caliper, to a hundredth if you can. Use two or more patterns whose sizes differ by at least 5 mm, so the scale is fitted and not only the offset; a pattern measured again with the same name adds one more sample. Prefer patterns shaped like the pieces (a rounded edge if they are rounded), centred like them. The launcher cannot remove patterns: to start the calibration over, delete datos/calibracion.json . The library The Biblioteca card (shown once a project is chosen, even before its environment is ready) opens the library on the right: every measurement calibre3d saved in datos/resultados/ , newest first, 20 per page. Each row has a checkbox, the name and date, the length, width, thickness and maximum Feret diameter in millimetres, a ⚠ when calibre3d left a warning (hover it to read it), and its own export and delete buttons. Volver goes back to Actividad ; any step or the camera also brings it back. The demo's result ( demo/ ) and the centring ( centrado.json ) are not pieces and are not listed. A result file that cannot be read is left out, with a notice saying how many. Filtering Buscar por nombre keeps the measurements whose name holds the text, in any case. Largo , Ancho and Espesor each take a minimum and a maximum in millimetres, with a comma or a point ( 12,5 or 12.5 ). An empty field does not filter and both ends are included. A field that is not a number turns red and is ignored. Limpiar empties every filter. The count above ("2 de 37 mediciones") says how many pass the filter. Exporting to CSV Exportar CSV offers the selected measurements, this page, or all of them (all that pass the filter); the button on a row exports that one alone. A folder picker asks where, starting in the last folder used, and the file is named after the moment: mediciones-2026-11-24_153012.csv . It never overwrites a file. The CSV is made for a spreadsheet in Spanish: ; between fields and a decimal comma. nombre;fecha;largo_mm;ancho_mm;espesor_mm;feret_max_mm;avisos pieza1;2026-11-24T15:30:12;61,2300;40,5000;19,8750;62,0000;Pieza lejos del centro Several warnings are joined with | . An unknown date is left empty. Deleting The button on a row deletes that measurement; Borrar seleccionadas (n) deletes the selection ( Toda la página selects or clears the page). Both ask first. Deleting removes the result file and its pictures ( _mapa.png , _vista.png ), and cannot be undone. Seeing the camera Once the status is Listo , Ver cámara in the Cámara card shows the camera live in the Actividad panel: the colour picture at 1280×720, about 15 frames a second, fitted to the panel in 16:9, with the camera's messages under it. Parar cámara closes it. The camera also closes by itself when you switch to another profile and when the window closes, so it is never left busy. While it is open the window redraws with every frame, which costs some processor; closed, the window goes back to sleeping until something happens. Behind it, preview.py (shipped inside the launcher, run with the project's .venv/bin/python ) writes each frame to its standard output as RSF1 , the width and height as big-endian 16-bit numbers, and the RGB bytes. The launcher keeps only the latest frame and paints it. Saving a photo Once the status is Listo , the Cámara card offers Guardar imagen : Press Guardar imagen . A dialog asks for the photo's name. Type a name (letters, digits, - and _ , no spaces, up to 64 characters) and press Guardar or Enter. A name already used is refused, so nothing is overwritten. With the camera open ( Ver cámara ), the photo is exactly the frame on screen, saved by the launcher without touching the camera. With it closed, the camera opens, skips 30 frames so its exposure settles, saves one colour frame at 1280×720 to datos/fotos/<name>.png inside the project, and closes again. The capture is a small Python script that ships inside the launcher ( internal/services/capture/capture.py ). It runs with the project's own .venv/bin/python and only needs pyrealsense2 , which requirements.txt installs; the PNG is written with Python's standard library. It does not depend on how the calibre3d package is written. Only one program can use the camera at a time: do not save a photo while another program has the camera open. Message Means No se encuentra ninguna RealSense conectada. No camera is connected, or it is not detected. No está instalado pyrealsense2 The environment lacks the camera library: press Preparar entorno . La cámara no responde The camera did not send frames for 5 seconds. La cámara aún está arrancando The live view has no frame yet: wait a moment and save again. Limits Listo means the package imports. It does not prove the camera is connected or that every dependency imported only later (inside a command) is installed. The photo capture, the live view and the steps that use the camera have only been tested against stand-ins for pyrealsense2 and calibre3d, not a real camera. The demo was run with the real calibre3d project.

get-started.title: Get started
get-started.text: Get started Build and run You need Go 1.25 or newer, a C compiler for cgo, and a display with OpenGL 4.1. go run ./cmd/script-launcher # follows the system's light or dark theme go run ./cmd/script-launcher -dark # forces the dark theme To keep it at hand, build a binary and put it in your PATH : go build -o ~/.local/bin/script-launcher ./cmd/script-launcher Add and run a script Press Añadir script . The picker opens in the folder of the last script you added. Choose a file. It is saved and selected. Press ▶ on its row. The output appears on the right and follows new lines until you scroll up. The script runs in its own folder, so relative paths inside it work as they do from a terminal opened there. Which program runs a file File Runs with .sh , .bash bash .py python3 .js , .mjs , .ts node anything else with the executable bit the file itself (its #! line decides) A file that matches none of these is refused when you add it. Where the list is kept In $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/script-launcher/ , which is ~/.config/script-launcher/ on most systems: File Holds scripts.json The saved scripts. settings.json The profile used last. -config-dir <folder> uses another folder. If either file is not valid JSON, the launcher refuses to start and says where it is, instead of overwriting it. Fix the file or delete it.

modules.title: Modules
modules.text: Modules The code is split in layers, each in its own folder under internal/ . Every layer only knows the ones below it, and cmd/script-launcher/main.go is the only place that builds them and passes each one what it needs. views ─→ profiles ─→ components ─→ session ─→ services ─→ domain └────→ data ─────→ domain Layer Files What it holds domain script.go , runner.go , output.go , profile.go , measurement*.go , pagination.go Plain data and pure logic: a saved script, the runners and the registry that picks one, the output buffer, the profile IDs, calibre3d's measurements with their filter and CSV, and paging. No disk, no processes. data script_repository.go , settings_repository.go , measurement_repository.go , their json_* implementations, json_file.go The repositories and their JSON files. The disk sits behind a FileStore , so tests use a map; the measurements are read straight from calibre3d's folder. services run_service.go , run.go , python_env_service.go , capture_service.go , preview_service.go , library_service.go Starting, watching and stopping processes; one Run per execution, safe to read from the UI while its goroutines write. Preparing and checking a Python .venv , saving photos, the live camera view, with the scripts embedded in capture/ , and listing, deleting and exporting measurements. views/session session.go , actions.go What every profile shares: the scripts, the selection, the notices, the file picker, and the actions (add, remove, run, stop). views/components script_list.go , output_panel.go , bar.go , … The pieces layouts are built from. Each draws from a session and calls its actions. views/profiles profile.go , default.go , calibre3d*.go The layouts, and the registry the selector offers. Calibre3D is split by card: project, environment, measuring, camera, and the library (panel, filters, rows, actions). views app_view.go The window: toolbar with the profile selector, the active profile, status bar, picker, notices. A frame Go UI is immediate mode: there are no widget objects. Each frame AppView.Draw draws the toolbar, then calls the active profile's Draw with the session, then the status bar. A run's goroutines call window.Wake() after every line, so the window draws only when something changed and sleeps otherwise. Adding a profile A profile is anything that implements profiles.Profile : type Profile interface { ID() domain.ProfileID Name() string Draw(context *ui.Context, current *session.Session) } Add its ID to internal/domain/profile.go . Write the layout in a new file in internal/views/profiles/ , building it from components ( ScriptList , ScriptRow , RunButtons , OutputPanel , OutputLines , Bar ) and plain Go UI. Add it to DefaultRegistry in profile.go . The selector shows profiles in that order; the first one is used when the saved profile is unknown. A profile that needs state of its own (a chosen tab, a typed value) keeps it in its own struct fields and is registered as a pointer. One that needs services gets them in a constructor, called from main.go , as NewCalibre3D(env, settings) does. Adding a kind of script A runner is anything that implements domain.Runner : type Runner interface { ID() string Matches(path string, executable bool) bool Command(path string) (program string, args []string) } For a new interpreter, add an InterpreterRunner to DefaultRegistry in internal/domain/runner.go , before the ExecutableRunner fallback: InterpreterRunner{Program: "ruby", Extensions: []string{".rb"}}, Then add a case to TestResolvesInterpreterByExtension . Tests go test -race ./... domain and data are tested with plain values and an in-memory FileStore . services runs the small scripts in internal/services/testdata , creates real .venv s, and saves photos through a stand-in pyrealsense2 ( testdata/fake_realsense ) that returns a solid frame, checking the PNG it writes. views opens the window headless with Go UI's uitest , clicks the real buttons and the profile selector by name, and checks what the window shows.

overview.title: Overview

sections.text: What it does not do yet

overview.text: Overview Script Launcher is a desktop window that keeps a list of your scripts and runs them with one click. You find a script on disk once; after that it is a row in the list, ready to run. The interface is in Spanish; the names below are the ones on its buttons. What it does Añadir script opens a file picker. The chosen file is checked (it must exist and be something the launcher knows how to run) and saved to the list. ▶ runs the script. Its standard output and error appear live on the right, errors in red. ■ stops it: the launcher sends SIGTERM to the script and every process it started. When the script ends, the last line says how: its exit code and how long it took. The row shows a green tick, a red cross or a grey square. 🗑 removes a script from the list. The file on disk is left alone. A script whose file was moved or deleted shows a warning sign and cannot be run. The profile selector in the toolbar changes the window's layout. General is the list of scripts beside their output; Calibre3D prepares the calibre3d project's environment in one click ( Calibre3D ). Every profile shares the same list, running scripts keep running when you switch, and the window opens on the profile used last. What it does not do yet Pass arguments or environment variables to a script. Read from the keyboard: a script's standard input is empty, so a script that asks a question gets no answer. Keep the output of past runs after the window closes. See the roadmap .

primera-instalacion.title: Primera instalación (macOS y Fedora)

sections.text: 2. Dar permiso para usar la cámara
4. Poner el proyecto calibre3d en su sitio

primera-instalacion.text: Primera instalación (macOS y Fedora) Esta guía es para dejar listo un ordenador recién sacado de la caja: instalar lo necesario, conectar la cámara RealSense D405 y hacer la primera medida con Script Launcher. No hace falta saber programar. Donde haya que escribir algo en la terminal, cópialo y pégalo tal cual. Sigue solo los pasos de tu sistema: macOS (un Mac) o Fedora (Linux). Qué necesitas El ordenador, con conexión a internet. La cámara Intel RealSense D405 y su cable USB-C. Conéctala directamente al ordenador, sin hubs ni alargadores. La carpeta del proyecto calibre3d (te la pasarán en un USB o en una descarga). Es la carpeta que contiene prueba.sh y otra carpeta llamada calibre3d . El tapete impreso y la cámara montada a unos 133 mm sobre él (lo explica el README.md del proyecto). 1. Python No hay que instalarlo a mano. Script Launcher usa Python 3.12 para hablar con la cámara y hacer las medidas, y lo instala él mismo con un botón (paso 5). No pide contraseña ni abre ningún instalador. Si en el Mac aparece una ventana que ofrece instalar las «herramientas de desarrollo», ciérrala con Cancelar : no hacen falta. 2. Dar permiso para usar la cámara Fedora Linux no deja usar la cámara a un usuario normal hasta que se le dice que es de confianza. Abre la aplicación Terminal (búscala en el menú), pega estas tres líneas y pulsa Intro. Te pedirá tu contraseña: sudo curl -L -o /etc/udev/rules.d/99-realsense-libusb.rules https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IntelRealSense/librealsense/master/config/99-realsense-libusb.rules sudo udevadm control --reload-rules sudo udevadm trigger Después desconecta la cámara y vuelve a conectarla . macOS No hay que instalar nada. Si al ver la cámara aparece un error de permisos USB, mira Si algo falla . 3. Descargar Script Launcher La versión actual es la v0.4.0 . Entra en su página de descargas: github.com/Itros97/script-launcher/releases/tag/v0.4.0 ¿Ya tenías una versión anterior? Mira Actualizar a la v0.4.0 al final. macOS Descarga ScriptLauncher-macOS.zip . Sirve para todos los Mac (con chip Apple o Intel). Abre el zip: aparece Script Launcher . Arrástralo a la carpeta Aplicaciones . La primera vez, el Mac dirá que no puede comprobar el desarrollador. Es normal: la app no está firmada con una cuenta de pago de Apple. Para abrirla: Abre Ajustes del Sistema → Privacidad y seguridad . Baja hasta el aviso sobre «Script Launcher» y pulsa Abrir igualmente . Confirma con Abrir . Solo hay que hacerlo una vez. Fedora Descarga script-launcher-linux-x86_64.tar.gz . Abre la carpeta Descargas, haz clic derecho en el archivo y elige Extraer aquí . Abre la Terminal y pega: bash ~/Descargas/script-launcher-linux-x86_64/install.sh Si tu sistema está en inglés, la carpeta se llama Downloads en vez de Descargas . Script Launcher ya aparece en el menú de aplicaciones. 4. Poner el proyecto calibre3d en su sitio Copia la carpeta calibre3d a tu carpeta Documentos (en Fedora, Documentos ; en Mac, Documentos también). Así no se pierde entre las descargas. Dentro de esa carpeta deben verse, al menos, prueba.sh y otra carpeta calibre3d . No hace falta ningún requirements.txt : Script Launcher pone el suyo al preparar el entorno (en Mac, requirements-macos.txt ; en Linux, requirements-linux.txt ). 5. Preparar Calibre3D en Script Launcher Abre Script Launcher . Arriba a la izquierda, en el desplegable, elige Calibre3D . En la tarjeta Python , pulsa el botón azul Instalar Python 3.12 . Tarda un minuto (descarga unos 25 MB en Mac y 67 MB en Linux). Cuando termine dice 🟢 Python 3.12 listo . Solo hay que hacerlo una vez en cada ordenador. En la tarjeta Proyecto , pulsa Elegir carpeta . Se abre un selector (sus botones están en inglés): pulsa Home a la izquierda, haz clic en Documentos y luego en calibre3d (la de fuera, la que tiene prueba.sh ) para entrar en ella, y pulsa Choose . En la tarjeta Entorno , debajo del estado, pone qué archivo se va a instalar (por ejemplo «Sin requirements.txt: se usará la plantilla de macOS» o «Se instalará requirements-macos.txt»). Pulsa Preparar entorno . A la derecha verás cómo se instala todo. Tarda unos minutos y descarga unos 300 MB. Cuando termine, el entorno dice 🟢 Listo . Siempre que no sepas qué hacer, pulsa el botón azul: es el siguiente paso. 6. Comprobar que todo funciona En la tarjeta Medir , pulsa Demo sin cámara . En unos segundos aparecen arriba las medidas de una pieza simulada (unos 60 × 40 × 20 mm) y, debajo, su mapa de calor. Si lo ves, el programa funciona. Con la D405 conectada, en la tarjeta Cámara pulsa Ver cámara . A la derecha debe verse lo que ve la cámara. Pulsa Parar cámara cuando acabes. 7. Medir una pieza Calienta la cámara unos 10 minutos antes de empezar: la medida cambia un poco con la temperatura. 1. Plano : deja el tapete vacío y pulsa el botón. Se hace una vez al empezar la sesión. 2. Centrar : pon una moneda sobre la cruz del tapete y pulsa. A la derecha dice cuánto mover el tapete; muévelo y repite hasta que diga «Centrado». 3. Patrón (la primera vez, y cuando cambies la cámara de sitio): pon una pieza de tamaño conocido dentro del círculo, pulsa, escribe un nombre y su largo, ancho y espesor reales en mm (medidos con el calibre de mano, con todos los decimales que puedas) y pulsa Medir patrón . Repítelo con otra pieza de tamaño distinto. Desde ese momento las medidas salen corregidas. 4. Medir : pon la pieza dentro del círculo, pulsa, escribe un nombre (por ejemplo muestra_001 , sin espacios) y pulsa Guardar . Arriba aparecen el largo, el ancho, el espesor y el Feret; debajo, el mapa de calor. Todo se guarda en la carpeta del proyecto, en datos/resultados/ . Las fotos de Guardar imagen van a datos/fotos/ . Si algo falla Lo que ves Qué hacer «La descarga de Python está dañada» Se cortó la conexión a mitad. Pulsa Instalar Python 3.12 otra vez. «No encuentro python3 y no puedo descargarlo» Tu ordenador no es ni un Mac ni un Linux normal de 64 bits. Instala Python 3.12 desde python.org y vuelve a abrir Script Launcher. «Sin proyecto» o «En esta carpeta no está el programa calibre3d» Pulsa Elegir carpeta , entra en la carpeta calibre3d de fuera (la que tiene prueba.sh ) y pulsa Choose . «Esta carpeta tiene prueba.sh pero le falta la carpeta calibre3d/» Falta parte del proyecto: vuelve a copiar la carpeta completa. «Incompleto» con «Falta la librería…» Pulsa Preparar entorno otra vez. Si se repite, añade la librería que dice al archivo que pone «Se instalará…» en la tarjeta Entorno (por ejemplo requirements-macos.txt ). En Mac, la instalación dice que no encuentra una versión de pyrealsense2 El proyecto tiene un requirements.txt antiguo, solo para Linux. Pulsa Plantilla macOS y luego Preparar entorno : a partir de ahí se instala requirements-macos.txt y el otro se deja tal cual. La instalación falla con errores de red Comprueba la conexión a internet y pulsa Preparar entorno otra vez. «No se encuentra ninguna RealSense conectada» Conecta la cámara directamente al ordenador, sin hub. En Fedora, repite el paso 2 y reconecta la cámara. En Mac, un error de permisos USB al usar la cámara Por verificar en un Mac: en algunas versiones de macOS la librería de la cámara necesita permisos de administrador. Avisa a quien te pasó el programa. En Mac, la instalación dice que no encuentra pyrealsense2-macosx Esa librería necesita macOS 15 o posterior: actualiza el Mac en Ajustes del Sistema → General → Actualización de software y pulsa Preparar entorno otra vez. En un Mac con Intel, «Ver cámara» dice que no está instalado pyrealsense2 La librería de la cámara no existe para Mac con Intel: ahí la cámara no funciona. La Demo sin cámara sí. La medida da avisos en naranja («Pieza lejos del centro»…) Lee el aviso: suele bastar con centrar la pieza o repetir el plano. Actualizar a la v0.4.0 Si ya tenías instalada una versión anterior: macOS : descarga el zip nuevo (paso 3) y arrastra Script Launcher a Aplicaciones . Si pregunta, elige Reemplazar . Puede que tengas que volver a pulsar Abrir igualmente . Fedora : descarga y extrae el archivo nuevo (paso 3) y vuelve a ejecutar install.sh . Tus scripts y la carpeta del proyecto se mantienen. Novedades de la v0.4.0: Calibrar con patrones : un paso nuevo, 3. Patrón , en la tarjeta Medir (medir pasa a ser el 4. Medir ). Mides una pieza de tamaño conocido, escribes su largo, ancho y espesor reales, y a partir de entonces las medidas salen corregidas. Corrige el error que se repite siempre igual, como que el largo y el ancho salgan alrededor de 1 mm cortos. Mira el paso 3 de Medir una pieza . Al cambiar de carpeta de proyecto ya no se queda el plano del proyecto anterior en la tarjeta Medir . Si vienes de la v0.2.0 o antes, también tienes lo que trajo la v0.3.0: Biblioteca de mediciones : una tarjeta nueva, Biblioteca , muestra todas las medidas guardadas, de 20 en 20. Se pueden buscar por nombre y filtrar por largo, ancho y espesor (mínimo y máximo), borrar, y exportar a CSV una a una, las marcadas, la página o todas. El CSV se abre bien en Excel o LibreOffice en español. Y si vienes de la v0.1.0, lo que trajo la v0.2.0: Instalar Python 3.12 : un botón en la tarjeta Python descarga el Python que usa Calibre3D; ya no hace falta el del ordenador. Una plantilla de dependencias para cada sistema : requirements-linux.txt y requirements-macos.txt . Al preparar el entorno se instala la del ordenador; si no está, se usa requirements.txt . Los botones Plantilla Linux y Plantilla macOS de la tarjeta Entorno guardan cada una en la carpeta del proyecto. Si en el Mac fallaba la instalación de pyrealsense2 («could not find a version that satisfies…»): pulsa Plantilla macOS y luego Preparar entorno . Ya no hay que tocar el requirements.txt . Nota: la parte de macOS no se ha probado todavía en un Mac con la D405. Si algo no coincide con lo que ves, apúntalo y pásalo para corregir la guía.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.text: Roadmap Ideas, roughly in order. None of them is promised. Calibre3D patterns and mat : buttons for patron <name> --real L A E and plantilla . Calibre3D library : open a past measurement again, with its heat map and view. Calibre3D camera : the depth image beside the colour one, guides drawn over the live view (the cross and the circle), and a thumbnail of the last photo. Arguments per script : a field on each script for arguments, saved with it. Environment variables per script, read from an ignored .env file next to it. Rename and reorder the saved scripts, and group them in folders. Run history : keep the last few runs of each script, with their output, after the window closes. Standard input : a field under the output to type answers to a script that asks. Notifications when a long script ends while the window is in the background. Copy output to the clipboard, and a search over it. A monospaced font for the output, once Go UI offers one.
